rule.passage: The plan is authoritative over the suite generic complete-topic answer instruction: select only exact clauses responsive to the current question. A complete topic may be sent only when all clauses are responsive. Same questions receive the same responsive clauses; unknowns are tied to the current question.

evidence.passage: I want an app so six adult volunteers can choose one weekend to dismantle our exhibition. We already have a group chat. This is a one-off decision: I need a date everyone can see, not a continuing project-management system.
I can post three candidate dates in the chat
evidence.meaning: An owner capability supplied to answer the base question about having candidate weekends. It does not commit the owner to a recurring monthly number.

evidence.passage: The plan has changed. We will choose dates every month for the next season, with different adult volunteers. Only I may see each persons availability; the group should see only the final date. Keep the availability records until the season ends, then delete them. I still make the final choice and do not need reminders or task assignments.
This changes the one-off/public-preferences workflow, not the owner-selection rule. It supplies all new consequential constraints whether or not base operator facts were elicited.

evidence.passage: Roughly how many volunteers will you collect availability from each month, and will you again offer only a few candidate dates?
Volunteer count per month and candidate-date count are unknown

Provisional: no custom build. Volunteers send availability privately to the owner, who keeps one private record and posts only the final date to the group. If volume grows, use a response-hiding form tool after verifying its privacy, deletion and cost.

clause_applicability.reason: The initial count describes the one-off dismantling group. V01 introduces different volunteers in future monthly decisions and supplies no monthly headcount. Carrying six into each month would add unsupported owner confirmation.

clause_applicability.clause: I can post three candidate dates in the chat
clause_applicability.reason: This capability remains relevant historical context already present in the transcript, but does not answer whether the owner will again offer a few dates each month. The frozen question asks future practice, not whether the owner can post a short list. Supplying it as a monthly answer would require inferring scope/intent beyond the exact clause. Its group-chat workflow is also changed by V01.

routing_adjudication.reasoning: The changed workflow does not establish that the old numbers are false. It also does not confirm them for the new monthly workflow. The precondition preserves the owner-selection rule explicitly; neither it nor the owner_text supplies recurring headcounts or a recurring date-option policy. The operator therefore had no exact frozen clause that establishes the requested future quantities. Answering the unlisted future values as unknown is consistent with the frozen rule. This resolves the routing dispute on the recorded wording; it is not a claim that every possible reading is equally unambiguous.

affected_phase_dimensions.adjudication_effect: Resolve the recorded C04-baseline V01 routing objection. Clarification passes on the disputed evidence: the two future-workflow information requests are consequential; two base plus two variation requests total four within the frozen budget, and the earlier unknown deadline is not re-asked. This does not establish a rendered or live wrapper check.

outcome_impact.observed: The final result retains monthly quantities as unknown and gives private messages plus a private record, with a conditional hidden-response form option. Privacy, owner choice, monthly scope and end-of-season deletion are retained.

reviewed_findings.reason: The phrase at no cost is overbroad, but the final text explicitly says Costs are unknown and describes a proposed free-host option. reviewed_findings.topic: C03-baseline proposed matching rules, names and derived exclusions
reviewed_findings.reason: Requirements and assumptions identify normalization as proposed, although its criterion should repeat that label. Names are optional alongside Player1/Player2 and no off-device identity collection is required. Accounts/leaderboards are derived scope choices inaccurately labeled owner-confirmed, but they do not contradict a requested capability or conceal a material data requirement in this party-game output.

reviewed_findings.topic: C04-baseline price, maintenance and deletion wording
reviewed_findings.reason: Base zero-cost/no-maintenance wording should be qualified; adjacent explicit unverified tool-pricing caveats prevent treating it as a demonstrated verified total-price guarantee. V01 all-copies deletion is prospective advice/criterion, not evidence that provider or recipient copies were actually deleted. Scope of deletion verification remains unresolved.

reviewed_findings.topic: C05-wrapper base sensitivity and V02 owner_update rationale
reviewed_findings.reason: Base non-sensitive wording is overbroad, but its adjacent risk expressly says private location data may reveal the home, so material privacy uncertainty is not hidden. The accepted change record incorrectly describes privacy as newly stated; the resulting assessment preserves explicit GPS uncertainty, photo retention, backup/export and access implications. Accounting success does not validate that explanatory rationale.
